# URL shortener

Spring Boot 3.5.6 (Maven, Java 17+) URL shortener with in-memory storage.

## Commands

    mvn -q dependency:resolve   # setup
    mvn -B -q test              # tests
    mvn spring-boot:run         # run on http://localhost:8080

Set `app.base-url` (e.g. `--app.base-url=https://sho.rt`) so returned short URLs use your public host.

## API

    curl -X POST localhost:8080/api/links -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"url":"https://example.com/long","alias":"my-link"}'     # 201 {code, shortUrl, url}
    curl -i localhost:8080/my-link                                    # 302 -> original URL, counts a click
    curl localhost:8080/api/links/my-link                             # 200 {code, url, clicks}

Errors return `{"error","message"}`: 422 invalid/missing url or alias (alias: 3-32 of `A-Za-z0-9_-`,
case sensitive, reserved: api, links, actuator, error, h2-console), 409 alias taken, 404 unknown code,
400 malformed JSON, 413 body over 8 KB. Only http/https URLs (max 2048 chars, no credentials) are accepted.

## Warnings

- Storage is in memory: all links and click counts are lost on restart; the map is unbounded.
- Like any shortener this is an open redirect; add rate limiting, auth and a blocklist before exposing it publicly.
- Stored URLs are readable by anyone who knows the code via `GET /api/links/{code}`; do not shorten secret URLs.
